dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.body: The dashboard shows the status for all running services. A green dot means OK, red means there's a problem. Press «Refresh» for the latest status.
dashboard.item_1: Green dot = service is responding normally
dashboard.item_2: Red dot = service is down or unreachable
dashboard.item_3: The model card shows the active AI model and latest response time
dashboard.item_4: The «Refresh» button fetches fresh status from all services

users.title: Users
users.body: Each family member has their own account with a role, PIN and individual permissions. The role determines what Kåre can help with.
users.roles_intro: The user role determines what Kåre can help with:

roles.child: Child — Limited to child-friendly content. No smart home control.
roles.teen: Teen — Internet access and more of Kåre, with some restrictions.
roles.young_adult: Young adult — Full access except admin functions.
roles.adult: Adult — Full access to all user features.
roles.admin: Admin — Controls the entire system, including settings and other users.
roles.household: System role for «Household (unrecognised voice)»: a person inside the house who isn't recognised, most likely a household member. Sees what the house shares (who lives here, shared lists, whether the house is set to away) but no individual's profile, memory, chats or notes. Tools are set in the table under Users.
roles.stranger: System role for «Unknown person»: a person we don't trust, e.g. at an outdoor or door node, and anything that can't be tied to a known user. Learns nothing about the house or its people, only sees the conversation in progress, and has no HA control by default.

users.vpn_intro: VPN access level determines what the user can do from outside the home network:

vpn.local_only: Local only — VPN access is blocked for this user.
vpn.ai_only: Kåre only — Can chat via VPN, but cannot control smart home.
vpn.full_access: Full access — Can do everything via VPN, including smart home control.

users.tools_intro: Tools are actions Kåre can perform. Under Settings → Agent settings you choose what each role has access to:

tools.ha_control: Turn lights, heating and other HA devices on/off
tools.ha_read: Fetch status from sensors and devices in the smart home system
tools.get_weather: Fetch weather forecast for home location
tools.web_search: Search the internet via DuckDuckGo, SearXNG or Brave
tools.kare_image: Generate images with AI (FLUX via HuggingFace)
tools.media: Play music, radio and Plex content
tools.note: Write and read notes in Kåre's notepad
tools.announce: Send voice announcements to speakers in the house
tools.reason_freely: Kåre thinks carefully through complex questions
tools.memory: Search and retrieve older conversations from long-term memory
tools.camera: See what the cameras have stored: pictures, episodes, search and who/what/where.
tools.camera_analyse: Start a new analysis with the image model (uses the graphics card). Can be turned off per role, for example for children.
tools.search_argus: Search system log and event history
tools.self_trace: View own response history for self-improvement; «recent» lists the user's own latest requests with real rids
tools.household: Set home/away mode for the household
tools.write_reflex: Suggest, approve or reject Kåre's self-learned automations (who can actually approve/reject is governed separately under Settings → Kåre)

users.pin: PIN is a numeric code that protects the account (minimum 6 digits). Used for login and to unlock private meeting minutes.
users.recovery_key: The recovery key is a 24-word recovery phrase shown once at account creation. It lets a user recover access to encrypted data if the PIN is forgotten — without it, encrypted data is lost for good. Can be re-issued here.
users.voice_reg: Voice registration lets Kåre recognise who is speaking. The user reads a few sentences and Kåre learns the voice profile.
users.vpn_qr: The VPN QR code contains all settings for connecting to the home network from outside. Scan it in the WireGuard app.
users.frigate_tracking: «Frigate may track me» (edit user, My settings, My children): link the person to their names in Frigate's face library. When the choice is No, KTSB removes the name from Frigate events as they come in — the event is kept as an anonymous «person». Adults and admins decide for themselves; for children and teens their guardians decide (an admin if no guardian is set). Applies to KTSB only: Frigate's own face library and Home Assistant are not changed, and old logs are not rewritten.
users.warning_delete: ⚠ Deleting a user is irreversible — all history and profile disappear permanently.
users.warning_vpn: ⚠ Deleting a VPN profile immediately removes external access for that user.
users.camera_questions: «Was it you?» (Settings, your own page): when the camera is unsure whether it was you, you get a question with only the camera and the time. The answers are your own — admin does not see them — and are stored in KTSB's weight system: one «yes» settles the event, and each face sensor that voted learns one small step (per camera and day/IR). «Private» = it was you, nothing more is kept. «Don't know» = the question is closed, no sensor learns anything, and KTSB does not ask less often because of it. «Skip» = KTSB asks less often. Anyone who turned camera tracking off is never asked. Kåre can also save your answer in the chat, one event at a time, and then shows the event's picture (same rules; never for an event with someone who opted out). Integrations → Frigate → Face sensors shows «learning: N of ~5 answers». Face sensors: Auto uses what KTSB learned from «Was it you?» answers once a sensor has about 5 answers on the same camera (5 is a fixed model constant, not a setting — so is the «Was it you?» list showing up to 5 questions, fewer when you skip). The switch «Auto uses what KTSB has learned» (on by default) covers all sensors; each sensor in Auto also has its own switch. A fixed word admin chooses always wins. The list also shows night-meeting themes about you that were set aside after three nights (only your own, never about others in the household). Kåre can put a camera event in your list himself instead of writing a note. In the chat (never voice) Kåre may put one question at a time from the list at the end of an answer after a light exchange (no command), with the event's picture as the camera pipe stored it — no analysis; «(no picture stored)» when there is none. How many a day (3 / 2 / 1 / 0) and at least an hour between are fixed model constants; if you answer he asks a little more often, if you leave it or skip, less. Switch: Integrations → Frigate → «Ask in the chat».
users.thing_questions: «Is this the same?» (Integrations → Frigate, admin): code proposes that a thing standing still on two cameras is the same when it has stood still at least 3 days on both and changed at the same time at least once. Code alone never gets past «uncertain»; only your yes links them. The place register is not changed.
users.place_questions: «What is here?» (Integrations → Frigate, admin only): KTSB counts, anonymously, where people appear or disappear in the middle of a camera's view – a door, a corner, a blind spot. A spot seen many times on several days becomes one question with the camera image and the spot marked. If you name it, KTSB can write «came from …» about events there. «Not a place» and «skip» stop the question. Nobody is counted by name. The cards «Was it you?», «Is this the same?» and «What is here?» always show: open questions on top (or «no open questions»), and a short history of the answers below. A place's image is a daytime recording frame with no active track on the camera – never a picture of a person; if there is none, the camera and position are shown as text. «Was it you?» never shows images.
users.questions_card: «Who / What / Where?» (one card): Who = «Was it you?» (on your own page and in the Frigate tab; only questions about yourself). What and Where are admin only for now (Integrations → Frigate): «What is this?» asks about things that stand still and are seen often (bins, cars, trailers, garden figures) and about things Frigate calls an animal although they never move. The answer is a name, «not a …», «wrong detection» or «skip». «Not a …» and «wrong detection» become a narrow rule (that camera, that label, that spot); the switch «Hold back confirmed wrong» (Frigate user card, default off) decides whether KTSB holds it back or only notes it. «Is this the same?» and «What is here?» as before. The card always shows the open questions and the answers so far, with pictures without people. Admin can also say who it was for others in the household (part «Who — others in the household», or in chat): only for someone who has not turned camera tracking off, and the person's own answer counts over admin's. Everything saved gives one receipt in a fixed form (what, where, who, channel, when), which Kåre repeats. Click a question to see the picture of the event; click again to close.
users.frigate_stills_view: «Latest detections» (Integrations → Frigate → episode list, the button above the list): every single-image read the image model already makes — L3 per event and each frame of the frame-by-frame run (module 4) — newest first, with the picture, the image model's own words, the step, time, camera and a link to the episode. Under each row, «The image model's words (raw)» unfolds the reply as the model gave it (up to ~4 KB), also when it could not be read — kept as long as the words. No extra model call.
users.frigate_modules: «Modules» (Integrations → Frigate): the camera pipe as modules 0–7. Module 1 (the old still-image analysis) is replaced by L3 per event and module 4. Modules 2 (Double Take), 4 (frame by frame), 5 (conclusion and memory) and 6 (the main model on doubt) can be switched here; 3 (the episode gate) follows the Frigate user. 4–6 are off by default: they use the main model, which on a small machine is the one Kåre answers with, so answers can get slower. With 5 off, an episode is closed by code with a short line and does not become a memory line.

vedlikehold.title: Maintenance
vedlikehold.body: Maintenance gives you control over Kåre's runtime without the terminal.
vedlikehold.item_1: Hot-reload — updates aliases and settings without a restart. Kåre stays available the whole time.
vedlikehold.item_2: Full restart — restarts the Kåre service. Takes 5–30 seconds.
vedlikehold.item_3: System check — verifies that all services respond and connections work.
vedlikehold.item_4: Memory compression — transfers short-term memory (STM) to long-term memory (LTM). Runs automatically each night.
vedlikehold.item_5: Backups — Create named backup points of the full installation (databases, memory, user keys and configuration). Restore from a saved point (PIN required) or download as ZIP. Max 5 points stored. Long-term memory includes conversations, knowledge, Kåre's drawers, the Frigate memory and the watch history; Images includes the kept Frigate episode frames (ordinary detection snapshots are cache and are not included). ⚠ Factory reset restores everything to defaults — requires PIN confirmation. The system key is never part of a backup: if you restore onto a new machine, each user has to log in with their PIN once before the background jobs (reflection, night job) can reach their data again.
vedlikehold.item_6: Update KTSB (Docker) — checks GitHub for newer versions and installs them with one click (PIN required). A backup point is saved automatically first (shown as «automatic» in the backup list, not counted against the 5). New images are checked against KTSB's signature before they are used. If something does not start properly, the previous version is put back on its own; an update never changes your data. Requires setup.sh / setup.ps1 to have been run in the install folder. Does not run while the night sequence is running.
vedlikehold.item_7: Include test versions (Expert) — below «Update KTSB». Off by default: only regular releases are offered. On: also test versions (rc) that come out before a regular release; they are signed and checked the same way, but less tested. When you run a test version, the regular release is offered either way.
vedlikehold.item_8: After saving, the settings pages say whether the change is in use at once («Saved and in use») or a service has to be restarted — then the service's name is shown with a link here, to Service restart.

verktoy.title: Tools
verktoy.summary: Insight into Kåre's tool usage and active timers
verktoy.body: The tools page provides insight into SSH nodes, timers and Kåre's action log. SSH connections to network machines are configured here.
verktoy.item_1: The timer overview shows active countdowns and reminders Kåre is tracking.
verktoy.item_2: The tool log shows the most recent actions Kåre has performed.
verktoy.item_3: You can see who asked for what, the timestamp, and whether it succeeded.

aliaser.title: Rooms and aliases
aliaser.summary: Where things are in the house, and the names Kåre knows them by
aliaser.body: The page has two tabs. Rooms is the source of truth for places and floors: with Home Assistant connected, rooms, floors and names come from there, and KTSB only adds synonyms, a location description and which devices Kåre should know. Aliases are the names people say — «the living room light» — and what they point at.
aliaser.item_1: Rooms — HA rooms (marked HA) and KTSB's own places (marked KTSB) for things that are not in HA, e.g. an MQTT sensor or a node. «Sync now» fetches from HA at once; otherwise KTSB follows changes in HA by itself.
aliaser.item_2: From HA — Rooms only (default): you add devices yourself, one by one, with + on a room. Pick myself: the same from the HA tree. As in Assist: what you exposed to HA's own voice assistant. Labelled in HA: what carries an HA label you choose. All (filtered): every ordinary entity, optionally only chosen types.
aliaser.item_3: Location description — where in the room a thing or node is, and what it watches (e.g. «on the cellar stairs»). Kåre uses it to tell things in one room apart.
aliaser.item_4: When a thing comes from HA, HA decides the room. If it is wrong, move the device in HA. Places you made yourself can be linked to an HA room with the same name.
aliaser.item_5: Aliases — grouped by the room the register gives the thing, colour-coded by type. «Without room» sits at the bottom in orange. Click a row, «Add» or + on a room to edit.
aliaser.item_6: Kåre understands both your synonyms and the HA names. When someone says «turn off the light» through a voice node, the node's room is used. «Turn off the lights on the second floor» only hits what is added to KTSB.

noder.title: Nodes
noder.summary: Audio and display devices Kåre can speak through or show content on
noder.body: A «node» is a device Kåre can speak through, display content on, or stream music to. Nodes have capabilities: Audio (TTS/announcements) and/or Display (images/text/video).

types.ha_media_player: HA Media Player — Device controlled by Home Assistant (Nest Hub, Google TV, smart speaker via HA)
types.esp32: ESP32 — Custom microcontroller board with speaker
types.wyoming: Wyoming — Voice satellites with microphone in and audio out (HA Voice protocol)
types.chromecast: Chromecast — Google Chromecast or Google TV, direct connection
types.snapcast: Snapcast — Synchronised multiroom audio over the local network
types.airplay: AirPlay — Apple protocol for wireless audio (HomePod, Apple TV, AirPlay speakers)
types.dlna: DLNA — Standard for wireless audio and pictures to compatible TVs and stereos. KTSB finds the device with a network search and remembers its address; in Docker on Windows/Mac the search does not get through — then enter the «DLNA description URL» under Channels on the node.
types.apple_tv: Apple TV — AirPlay-based, supports display and audio
types.samsung_tv: Samsung TV — Tizen OS, controlled via HA or directly
types.android_tv: Android TV — generic Android TV platform
types.google_tv: Google TV — Google's TV platform (Chromecast Gen 4+)
types.fire_tv: Fire TV — Amazon's TV platform (FireStick, Fire TV Cube)
types.lg_tv: LG TV — webOS, controlled via Home Assistant

noder.trust: Nodes with a microphone have a setting for who an unrecognised voice is. «Indoor» means probably someone in the household: Kåre answers as to «Household (unrecognised voice)», which gets what the house shares but no individual's own data. «Outdoor / at the door» means a stranger: Kåre answers as to «Unknown person», which learns nothing about the house and cannot control HA. A satellite that is not added here is treated as an unknown person.
noder.place: Place — every node stands at a place from Rooms and aliases (HA rooms first), with a location description. When someone asks for something through the node without saying where, Kåre uses the node's place. A node without a place is marked orange.
noder.lead_in: Silence before the reply — network speakers (HA media player, Chromecast/Nest) cut the first tenths of a second of a reply, and almost a second when the reply interrupts something playing. The voice bridge therefore puts silence first: 400 ms normally, 1200 ms when the speaker was playing. Both can be changed per node in the node dialog; 0 turns it off.
noder.channels: Channels (TVs and Cast devices): one node is one physical device, and it can be reached several ways at once — TvOverlay for a corner notice, Cast or DLNA for a full-screen picture, Home Assistant as a fallback, and the TV's own remote control. KTSB finds the channels itself by trying the ports when you save a new TV, or when you press «Search for channels» in the node dialog (Nodes → Edit). Each channel can be switched off there. Kåre says which channel was used, also when the first one did not answer. The WiFi icon shows which channels answer now. A Nest or Google Home that lives in Home Assistant can also get an IP address in the node dialog — KTSB then reaches it with its own Cast (pictures, NRK, web pages) and uses Home Assistant as the fallback. Remote control (Android TV and Samsung): press «Pair with TV» in the channel list — Android TV shows a code you type in, Samsung asks «Allow?» on screen. Kåre can then turn the TV on and off (true state, never fully shut down), change volume and mute, send keys (Home, Back, Pause …) and start apps — only when someone asks. Over its own Cast KTSB also plays a YouTube video you ask for (the code searches by itself; Nest Hub and Google TV) and NRK by name («today's Dagsrevyen» finds the newest episode). Pictures on a TV close by themselves after their time, unless something else was put on meanwhile. When a room has two screens (e.g. a Nest Hub and a TV), Kåre asks which one you mean — say «the TV» or «the Nest» and he picks right. The description you give the node helps him tell them apart.

kameraer.title: Cameras
kameraer.item_1: Cameras are set up under Integrations → Frigate.
kameraer.item_2: Analyse + Min. confidence — Per camera: ticked objects Frigate is at least this sure of make episodes and are analysed by KTSB. The rest is stored as plain events without model calls. Fire/smoke and «not welcome» are always included. «Can make episodes» on the camera card decides whether the camera can start a situation at all (default off for a road-facing camera, on for others). Plates Frigate reads are stored as claims and can join an open episode.
kameraer.item_3: Storage limit — Maximum number of images and total size (MB) Kåre stores per user.
kameraer.item_4: Snapshot — Kåre takes an instant photo from a camera on request.
kameraer.item_5: Events — Kåre fetches motion events and object detection from Frigate.
kameraer.item_6: Storage over time (Integrations → Frigate, Expert) — Nothing is deleted for being old. The camera events (frigate.db) have a size limit in the Storage limits card: over it the oldest details are slimmed first (in a situation) or deleted (outside one) — only what is already counted per hour and day — and when no details are left, the oldest hourly counts go. Daily counts, situations and visits are always kept. Dry run logs what the night job would delete without deleting. «Keep unknown plates»: 7 days or always.
kameraer.item_7: Likely false detection — Frigate's label («deer», «person») is a claim. When the vision model sees no person and no animal in the frames, code ends the episode as «likely false detection» without using the main model. Urgent cases (fire/smoke, not welcome, a person while you are away) always go to the main model. The weather around the episode (from Settings → Weather) is attached as facts.
kameraer.item_8: The camera memory cannot write — a red line at the top of Episodes means KTSB cannot store new events (e.g. wrong owner on frigate.db). Argus is told once when it happens and once when it works again.
kameraer.item_9: Vehicles (Integrations → Frigate → Who / What / Where, admin) — the same path as unknown people: a confirmed, unknown plate gets an anonymous id (V-…, never the plate number). Seen on several days it becomes a question with a picture; you give a household name and a class (household / safe guest / not welcome) or skip. Known plates have their name from Frigate. Until KTSB can read the plate from the picture itself, no plate counts as confirmed — so no ids are made from noise.

sikkerhet.title: Security
sikkerhet.summary: Camera events, anomalies, and home/away mode
sikkerhet.item_1: Event feed — Recent camera detections grouped by object and camera, with a snapshot thumbnail on row click.
sikkerhet.item_2: Deviation score — How unusual an event is compared to the last 28 days on the same camera, hour, and weekday. 0 = happens almost every time at this hour, 1 = has never happened at this hour before.
sikkerhet.item_3: Confidence — How much history Kåre has to base the deviation score on. Under roughly two weeks of data, the score isn't yet used in alert routing.
sikkerhet.item_4: Correction — Mark an event as normal or unusual. The correction feeds into next night's baseline recomputation.
sikkerhet.item_5: Home/away mode — When the household is set to "away", camera alerts escalate (especially unknown objects at perimeter cameras at night), and Kåre automatically detects when someone returns via GPS or local network presence.
sikkerhet.item_6: Undo and sorting — Click a column header to sort events within a group. After a correction (single or batch), a brief "undo" button appears and restores the previous state.

agenter.title: Agent Messages
agenter.body: Kåre does not work alone. Several agents contribute behind the scenes. This page shows messages and thoughts they have shared — read-only.
agenter.miss_kare: Miss Kåre — Evaluates Kåre's responses in real time. Adds side comments and alerts Kåre to inaccuracies. Runs on the 9B model.
agenter.miss_library: Miss Library — A dusty librarian AI. Searches local Wikipedia and the internet when Kåre needs facts.
agenter.mechanic: Mechanic — A technical assistant Kåre can delegate tasks to. Thinks independently and delivers answers.
agenter.jing: Jing — Kåre's fast inner voice. Scans HA events every 3 minutes and sends short thought fragments. Runs locally (OpenVINO/CPU) or on a remote machine.
agenter.jang: Jang — Kåre's deep, slow inner voice. Reads Jing's thought fragments every 10 minutes and updates Kåre's self-image. Runs locally or on a remote machine.

refleksjoner.title: Reflections
refleksjoner.body: Kåre holds two meetings every night. It is his way of learning from the day and growing as an assistant.
refleksjoner.item_1: Reflection meeting (nightly) — Kåre and Miss Kåre review the day's conversations. Kåre updates his self-description and world model.
refleksjoner.item_2: Dev slot (right after the reflection meeting) — Kåre goes through his agenda (things he noted himself as 'raise at the dev meeting'), Janus prioritises, Kåre investigates problems with read-only tools, and code plus a smaller model check that every finding has evidence. The morning report shows verified findings, suspicions and proposals. Every item gets a theme when it is written (by Kåre himself, or by fixed rules when he gives none), and the slot takes topics from all themes. Janus also sees resolved topics: when a new topic is the same as something already settled it is linked there as an echo; when new data contradicts the solution it becomes a reopen proposal you decide on.
refleksjoner.item_3: PIN protection — Meeting minutes are locked with the user's PIN. Only you can read your own minutes.
refleksjoner.item_4: Topic field — You can suggest a topic for Kåre to address in the next nightly meeting. For the dev slot you also pick which theme it belongs to (or let it be chosen automatically).
refleksjoner.item_5: Miss Kåre portrait — Miss Kåre notes short, dated observations about each user: things they actually said or did, traceable to a conversation. No interpretation of feelings or motives. The notes are included in the meeting context.
refleksjoner.item_6: Proposals from the dev slot — The slot never changes anything itself. Proposals are numbered in the report; an admin confirms or rejects them in chat ('confirm dev proposal 2'), and a human makes the actual change.
refleksjoner.item_7: Consolidation — When a week, month, half-year or year has ended, code counts what happened and Janus writes a short summary. Items left open for more than 7 days leave the active agenda once their week is summarised — they are never deleted.

innst_basic_expert.title: Settings → Basic/Expert toggle
innst_basic_expert.summary: One switch controls what shows on every tab
innst_basic_expert.body: At the top right of the Settings page there's a toggle labeled "Basic"/"Expert". It gates advanced fields across all tabs at once — not just one.
innst_basic_expert.item_1: Basic (default) — Shows only what an everyday household user needs: model name, temperature, on/off switches, location, etc. Technical settings (provider, timeouts, raw prompt text) are hidden.
innst_basic_expert.item_2: Expert — Shows everything, including vLLM/Docker parameters, role governance, advanced thresholds, and the Agent Settings tab (which is completely hidden in Basic mode).
innst_basic_expert.item_3: The setting is remembered in the browser (localStorage) and only affects visibility — never which values are actually stored in the configs/ files.

innst_generelt.title: Settings → General
innst_generelt.summary: Location, time zone, language and network, VPN
innst_generelt.item_1: Location — Home location used for weather, sunrise/sunset and geographic context. Stored locally.
innst_generelt.item_2: Time zone — Kåre uses this to understand time and date correctly.
innst_generelt.item_3: Language — Kåre's response language and GUI language. Choose between Norwegian, English and German.
innst_generelt.item_4: Network and access (Expert) — local and VPN subnets decide whether a user counts as at home. Trusted proxies are the only ones that may state the client's address; everything you set up yourself works, everything else is stopped. The API documentation (/docs) is off by default.
innst_generelt.item_5: Default local network — Without your own choice every 192.168.x.x address counts as home (not the Docker network 172.16–31.x and not the VPN subnet). The setup wizard suggests your own /24 from where you connect; you confirm or change it.
innst_generelt.item_6: WireGuard VPN — Lets you use Kåre securely from outside your home network. Generate QR codes for users on the Users page.
innst_generelt.item_7: DuckDNS — Free DNS service that gives your home a fixed domain name even if the IP address changes. Used by VPN.

innst_diskbruk.title: Settings → Logs/Storage
innst_diskbruk.summary: How much space KTSB may use, and logs and data
innst_diskbruk.item_1: Argus — indexed events: a limit in MB for Argus (0 = off). Nothing is deleted for being old; when the limit is reached, the oldest days are summarised and deleted first (at most 30 days per night, never today). The summary — counts per day, source, entity and level, and every warning and error verbatim — is kept for good in state/argus/rollup.db.
innst_diskbruk.item_2: Logs and data (Expert) — how often logs are written to disk (collected in memory; low = more I/O and SD-card wear, high = more can be lost in a power cut; 0 = at once) and how many days conversations and episodes are kept (0 = forever; older data is permanently deleted at night). Reply length in the think log: how much of each reply is kept next to the thinking (default 4000 characters, the thinking is always kept whole) — used to measure the model guard on long replies; the reply is stored as plain text.
innst_diskbruk.item_3: Storage per group — shows each disk («KTSB is set up to use x GB of y GB») and five groups: what you added, logs, Frigate pictures, Frigate text and Kåre's own files. Changing a group's limit scales its data types by the same factor. A warning when the limits on a disk exceed the disk. Expert shows every data type; those without a limit yet are marked «coming». Limits with their own place — Frigate (Integrations → Frigate → Storage limits) and images (Settings → Logs/Storage → Images) — are shown here but set there.
innst_diskbruk.item_4: Kåre's own files with a limit here: the think log, inner thoughts, conversation history (STM, one folder per day) and observations (per user). Over the limit the oldest goes first; an STM day is deleted only once its daily summary exists. What Kåre reads into the prompt is unchanged (observations: last 14 days; inner thoughts: only the newest). Miss Kåre's portraits stay at 3000 characters, because the whole portrait goes into her prompt. Raw HA and Frigate events are stored as one file per day; over the limit the oldest whole days are deleted each night (Frigate always keeps at least 28 days for the normalcy baseline). Argus and Kåre are not affected.

innst_ha.title: Integrations → Home Assistant
innst_ha.summary: Connection to the smart home hub
innst_ha.body: Home Assistant (HA) is the brain of the smart home system. Kåre uses HA to control lights, heating and sensors. Kåre can also control volume, source and pause on HA media players (speakers and TVs). «Turn the sound up» with nothing named means the speaker the replies to the node you speak through play on. Which actions Kåre may use is set under Integrations → Home Assistant → HA Gateway — Advanced Settings → Allowed actions (Expert mode).
innst_ha.item_1: HA URL — The address of Home Assistant on the local network (e.g. http://192.168.0.x:8123).
innst_ha.item_2: Token — A one-time key you create in HA under Profile → Long-lived access tokens. Kåre uses this to authenticate.
innst_ha.item_3: Timeout — How long Kåre waits for a response from HA. Increase if the network is slow.
innst_ha.item_4: Allowed actions — Checkbox list of the 11 actions Kåre can perform against HA (turn on/off, set level, color, temperature, etc). Lives under Expert level.
innst_ha.item_5: Home Assistant on/off — Off means Kåre controls no devices and reads no HA sensors. The setup wizard turns it on when URL and token are saved. A new URL or token takes effect immediately (the gateway reloads).
innst_ha.item_6: Wait for confirmation — After an action Kåre checks that the device actually changed (if HA does not have it, he says so and sends nothing). He waits until HA reports the new state, at most the seconds you set. Slow lights give «sent, not confirmed», never a false «done».

innst_mqtt.title: Integrations → MQTT
innst_mqtt.item_1: MQTT — Lightweight message protocol used by Frigate to send camera events to Kåre. Only needed if you use Frigate cameras.
innst_mqtt.item_2: MQTT broker — The server that relays MQTT messages. Usually the Mosquitto add-on in Home Assistant.

innst_llm.title: Settings → LLM / Models
innst_llm.summary: Kåre's AI brain and supporting models
innst_llm.body: LLM (Large Language Model) is the AI model that makes Kåre intelligent. Here you configure which models are used for what.
innst_llm.role_kare: Kåre — The main model. Answers every question. With 27B on a 24 GB+ GPU Kåre works as intended; with 9B or smaller (the default on a fresh install) it is basic mode — conversation works, tool use is unreliable. The card then shows a yellow note.
innst_llm.role_miss_kare: Miss Kåre — The evaluator model. Checks Kåre's responses. Runs on a dedicated GPU.
innst_llm.role_library: Miss Library — The library model. Searches wiki and the internet.
innst_llm.role_mechanic: Mechanic — Technical assistant. Shares hardware with Miss Kåre.
innst_llm.role_frigate: Frigate — The model that looks at camera images on Frigate events. Under Integrations → Frigate you choose who it borrows the model from: Main agent (Kåre's model, default) or Sub-agents (the agent model); in Expert also a model of its own (must understand images).
innst_llm.role_frigate_conclude: Frigate conclusion — The model that decides what a whole camera episode meant, and at once (with the image) for urgent cases. Under Integrations → Frigate you choose who it borrows the model from: Main agent (default) or Sub-agents; in Expert also a model of its own. Shadow mode: stored, nothing sent.
innst_llm.role_fallback: Fallback — Used if the main model is unavailable.
innst_llm.role_sky: Cloud — Cloud-based model (DeepSeek) as a safety net when local capacity is full.
innst_llm.item_1: Whisper — Turns your voice into text. Norwegian uses the National Library's NB-Whisper, other languages OpenAI's Whisper. Pick Small/Medium/Large, «Download», then «Use this» — or enter another model (Hugging Face name or link). Runs on the CPU; OpenVINO (Intel iGPU) is a manual Expert option outside Docker. Expert: CPU threads (Auto = half the cores, at most 8).
innst_llm.item_2: Embedding (BGE-M3) — Creates searchable vectors for the wiki and Argus. Can also serve as the «Large» model for semantic memory.
innst_llm.item_3: Local vs. cloud — Local models are faster and private. Cloud is a safety net if something fails.
innst_llm.item_4: num_ctx — The context window. How much of the conversation the model remembers in one run.
innst_llm.item_5: Piper (text-to-speech) — Kåre's voice. Three language sections (Norwegian/English/German) with different voice packs. Download, activate the desired voice and restart the service to apply it.
innst_llm.item_6: Reason Freely tool — Kåre's own free-reasoning tool, shown nested inside the Kåre (main) card since it shares the same model. Lives under Expert level.
innst_llm.item_7: Agent pool — Fallback, Miss Kåre, Miss Library and Mechanic run on the same small model and share one set of settings (thinking, context and sampling). Changing them on one card changes them for all four. Only max answer length is set per role. This keeps the model from reloading between jobs.
innst_llm.item_8: Model check — Every Ollama role is checked against the models actually downloaded. If the model is missing, a yellow warning shows on the card (and in the log at startup); the role won't work until the model is downloaded. «Can't reach» only means the instance didn't answer the check.
innst_llm.item_9: vLLM restart — Sampling (temperature, top_p, presence_penalty …) applies from the next message after saving, no restart needed. Docker parameters (context length, KV cache, GPU memory) need «Restart Docker container». The button re-creates the container and waits until the model has loaded (a few minutes). If the new one fails to start, the previous one is restored automatically.
innst_llm.item_10: Semantic memory — Lets Kåre find old conversations by meaning, also across Norwegian, English and German. Three sizes: Small (118 MB), Medium (1.1 GB, clearly better) and Large (uses the Embedding service). «Download», then «Use this»: memory search is rebuilt from stored conversations, nothing is deleted, and you can switch back.
innst_llm.item_11: Model storage (Expert) — The folder KTSB downloads models to. Default /kaare/models (in Docker: the models/ folder next to docker-compose.yml).
innst_llm.item_12: LAN address for speakers (Piper card) — The address speakers on your network fetch Kåre's audio from. Empty = detected automatically outside Docker; in Docker enter the machine's LAN address (the button suggests the address you opened KTSB on). Takes effect immediately.
innst_llm.item_13: Push URL for the inner voices (Inner voices card, Expert) — Where Jing and Jang send their thoughts when they run on another machine. Empty = they write straight into KTSB's files. With an address and the token, Jing also fetches who the cameras saw, as anonymous person ids (never names).
innst_llm.item_14: Jing and Jang (inner voices) — The models of Kåre's two inner voices. Empty address = off. Can point at this machine or another one in the house (OpenAI-compatible server); the API key is sent as Bearer and never shown in logs.

innst_refleksjon.title: Settings → Reflection
innst_refleksjon.item_1: Meeting leader style — The tone of the meetings: Standard, Strict, Exploratory or Custom.
innst_refleksjon.item_2: Enabled/Disabled — Temporarily turn off reflection meetings.
innst_refleksjon.item_3: Max rounds — Number of exchanges between Kåre and Miss Kåre per meeting.
innst_refleksjon.item_4: Jang interval — How often Jang sends thought messages to Kåre between meetings.
innst_refleksjon.item_5: Dev slot enabled — Turn the nightly dev slot on or off.
innst_refleksjon.item_6: Time budget — Safety ceiling for how many minutes the dev slot gets per night (default 25). What it does not reach is taken the next night.
innst_refleksjon.item_7: Max user turns — How many of yesterday's conversations Kåre reviews per night (default 20).
innst_refleksjon.item_8: Max tool rounds per topic — How thoroughly Kåre may investigate one problem (default 4).
innst_refleksjon.item_9: Night sequence → Start time — When the night work starts (default 03:00, household timezone). If the machine is off then, the night still runs if KTSB is back up within 6 hours. Applies from the next night.
innst_refleksjon.item_10: Topics per meeting — How many problems the dev slot investigates in depth per night (default 3). It first takes one topic from each theme (answers, tools, memory, agents, house, system, other) and then fills up, so one noisy area cannot take the whole meeting. Each topic takes a few minutes, so raise the time budget along with this.
innst_refleksjon.item_11: Max tokens (Kåre / Miss Kåre) — How much each may write per turn in the meeting. Applies to the meeting only; chat uses «Max tokens out» in the LLM tab. Thinking counts toward the cap, so Kåre needs far more than the turn itself: below about 3000 often gives empty replies, 6000–8192 is recommended. Miss Kåre does not think by default and manages with 1000–1500. Not the same as the context length (how much the model can read).

innst_nett.title: Settings → Web Search & Weather
innst_nett.summary: Search provider, weather and local sensors
innst_nett.item_1: Search engine — SearXNG (default, self-hosted, no key — ships with Docker) or Brave Search (API key). DuckDuckGo has been removed. Kåre can send a search off as a work round: he answers you at once and comes back in the chat with his own answer when the search is done (raw data is never shown directly and is not kept in short-term memory).
innst_nett.item_2: Weather provider — met.no, OpenWeatherMap, PirateWeather, WeatherAPI or local HA sensors.
innst_nett.item_3: Local HA sensors — Kåre can read indoor sensors (temperature, humidity) from Home Assistant.
innst_nett.item_4: Tide — Tide data from the Norwegian Mapping Authority (Norwegian coastal locations).
innst_nett.item_5: Whitelisted websites — the household's trusted sources get the places first and are labelled «trusted source»; the open web (can be switched off) fills the rest and is labelled as such. Each domain has a type and a trust level. Blocked websites are never used. Regardless of the list, KTSB never fetches pages on internal addresses (localhost, home network, VPN), obeys robots.txt, and refuses large or non-text files. Kåre says how likely something is with fixed words (highly likely / likely / uncertain / unlikely), computed by code from the kind of sources and how many independent ones agree; «How careful» moves the bar.
innst_nett.item_6: Norwegian law (Lovdata) — optional. Current laws and central regulations from Lovdata's open datasets (NLOD 2.0), downloaded once per night and searched locally; lovdata.no itself is never fetched (Lovdata blocks bots). Answers from the laws count as public authority and always credit Lovdata.

innst_bilder.title: Settings → Logs/Storage → Images
innst_bilder.summary: Image generation and storage limits (now in Logs/Storage)
innst_bilder.item_1: Kåre can generate images with AI (FLUX model via HuggingFace).
innst_bilder.item_2: Storage limit per user — Maximum number of images and total size (MB).
innst_bilder.item_3: Images are stored locally and only visible to the user who requested them.
innst_bilder.item_4: Old images are deleted automatically when the limit is reached (oldest first).

innst_kare.title: Settings → Assistant Settings
innst_kare.item_1: Assistant name — What Kåre is called in your home. Default is «Kåre», but you can choose freely.
innst_kare.item_2: Hotword — The activation word Kåre listens for to start voice recognition.
innst_kare.item_3: Personality mode — Determines the depth and tone of Kåre's responses:
innst_kare.item_4: Minimal — Extra fast. Short and concise answers, almost no personality.
innst_kare.item_5: Lightweight — Balanced. Friendly and helpful, but not too long.
innst_kare.item_6: Standard — Full personality with humour, honesty and curiosity.
innst_kare.item_7: Complete — Uses all context: inner thoughts, self-image and world model.
innst_kare.item_8: Custom — You write Kåre's personality yourself.
innst_kare.item_9: Who influences Kåre — Choose which users can shape Kåre's personality through conversations.
innst_kare.item_10: Kåre's self-learned automation — Choose who can approve or reject automation proposals Kåre suggests based on habits it notices around the home.
innst_kare.item_11: Kåre's memory (Assistant settings) — «Who can mark a topic resolved» (default: admin only): a topic settled in a conversation is locked, and new observations about the same become echoes. In Expert: «Relevant now» (notes that fit the message are attached in full text), number of hits and thresholds, caps for lessons, core facts and index, length per lesson, and the reminder list caps (length per note, max count). «Relevant now» needs an embedding service (LLM / Models → «BGE-M3 (Embeddings)» or «Semantic memory»); the card shows «Inactive» when the switch is on without one.

innst_integrasjoner.title: Integrations → Frigate and Plex
innst_integrasjoner.summary: Frigate camera NVR and Plex media server
innst_integrasjoner.item_1: Frigate — Camera NVR with AI detection. Kåre uses Frigate to take photos and fetch events.
innst_integrasjoner.item_2: Plex — Media server (NAS or PC). Kåre can search Plex and cast media to TV.
innst_integrasjoner.item_3: Plex token — Obtained from your Plex account and lets Kåre communicate with the server.
innst_integrasjoner.item_4: Connection — Shows whether KTSB is connected to Plex. «Connected» means Plex reports at once when something starts, pauses or stops; «Plex rejects the token» means you need to enter a new token here.
innst_integrasjoner.item_5: Plex account per person — Under Users → edit you choose which Plex account the person watches with. KTSB then keeps its own record of what they watched, where, and what comes next, next to what Plex itself says.
innst_integrasjoner.item_6: Cameras — Per-camera setup (analysis, objects, thresholds, minimum duration), storage and away mode are in the Frigate tab, below the connection. Most of it is Expert.
innst_integrasjoner.item_7: Face classification — Under Integrations → Frigate an admin chooses, for each face Frigate has learned, whether the person is household, safe guest or not welcome, and fills in a simple profile (beard, glasses, age, headwear; «don't know» is allowed). KTSB uses the profile to check whether Frigate's recognition matches the image. Unclassified faces count as unknown, and their name is kept only a limited number of days (Expert). Which KTSB user a face belongs to is linked on the Users page.
innst_integrasjoner.item_8: Frigate user (shadow mode) — The switch at the top of Integrations → Frigate. When on, KTSB checks the name Frigate gives a face against the image itself before anything is stored: faces that are too small, night images and low scores are not checked (the name is stored as "Frigate's claim, unverified"); a model describes the image without being told the name, and the code compares that with the face profile. One contradiction (e.g. a beard on someone without one) only raises a doubt: the name is stored as unverified, with the doubt visible. The name is dropped only when two images in the same situation agree on the contradiction. When a situation is over, the vision model sees up to nine frames from the whole situation in one call, while the code gives the route and the clock times (which cameras, in which order, in or out). Cameras with a role such as «Road facing» and cars that are only parked do not keep a situation open. Anyone who said no to tracking is never stored by name. Shadow mode: no alerts, nothing Kåre says changes yet. Time limits and thresholds are Expert settings.
innst_integrasjoner.item_9: Episodes — At the top of Integrations → Frigate. Each row is one situation across cameras: time span, the cameras in order, who Frigate said it was (with KTSB's check: confirmed / unverified — never fact) and the conclusion. Click for the frames the model saw, the route (from code), what the image model saw and any suggested alert — in shadow mode nothing is sent. Images come from Frigate's recordings and disappear when Frigate deletes them (usually after 7 days). Expert shows the claim check per event. The frames the model saw are stored on the KTSB machine (Storage limits at the bottom of the Frigate tab, Expert): over the episode-frames cap older episodes keep only their middle frame, and those have their own cap; 0 = not stored. A stored frame shows even after Frigate has deleted the recording.
innst_integrasjoner.item_10: Extra face recognition — Under Integrations → Frigate you can connect a second face recognition (first: Double Take over MQTT). It gives its own vote per Frigate event: when both agree the name becomes «very likely», when they disagree it becomes «uncertain», and KTSB checks the features in the image against both people. Disagreements go on the review list. Frigate's own MQTT topic now also sits in the Frigate tab, not the MQTT tab (which keeps only the broker connection).
innst_integrasjoner.item_11: Episodes: analysis and frames — The frames code picks for each episode are always kept, also when the vision model does not answer. If the vision model could not be reached, the episode shows «waiting for analysis» and KTSB tries again by itself (first on the other model instance, then with pauses). The «Analyse» / «Analyse again» button in the episode view (admin) re-runs the image check and the conclusion on the kept frames — Frigate is not needed. The previous conclusion stays under «Earlier conclusions». A conclusion without an image check is marked «Not checked with images». How often the button can be used is set under Integrations → Frigate → «Frigate user (shadow mode)» (Expert), default 2 per 10 minutes. If an episode is assessed again after its day is in long-term memory, the night writes a correction for it. An episode still open or without a conclusion longer than «Stuck after» (default 30 min) is marked «stuck» with what the code knows (queued, waiting for the image model, failed, analysis started at), and «Analyse again» becomes available.
innst_integrasjoner.item_12: Episodes: chapters and changes — Code splits a long episode into chapters where the situation really shifts: everyone has gone, someone reaches a new place, or the image stays still for a long time. The frames follow what happens: more where something changes, few in a calm stretch (up to 24 per episode; short episodes keep about 9). Under «Looks different after the episode» code compares frames before and after and says where something differs, not what. It only counts where someone has actually been, and not when a camera switches between colour and IR. No setting: Frigate's own motion masks apply.
innst_integrasjoner.item_13: Expressions and gestures — The image model describes facial expressions and gestures per frame in the episodes, in its own words, and only when the person is large enough in the image for the face or arms to be read. They appear in the timeline as the image model's words and reach the main model as what one frame showed. On by default (Integrations → Frigate). Each person can turn it off for themselves in the «Frigate may track me» card; for children and teens their guardians decide. If a recognised person in the episode has said no, nothing is asked for anyone in that episode. Someone who has opted out of tracking never has their name tied to anything.

innst_distribusjon.title: Settings → Distribution
innst_distribusjon.item_1: Profile — Full (GPU + all services), Medium (limited GPU) or Lightweight (CPU only).
innst_distribusjon.item_2: The profile determines which services are available, but not which LLM provider you use.
innst_distribusjon.item_3: Domains — Kåre's local and external addresses (for VPN and reverse proxy).
innst_distribusjon.item_4: Services — Shows which background services (embedding, wiki, Qdrant) are enabled.

innst_agenter.title: Settings → Agent Settings
innst_agenter.summary: Configure Mechanic and Miss Kåre's permissions
innst_agenter.item_1: Mechanic — Choose which tools Mechanic can use on behalf of Kåre.
innst_agenter.item_2: Miss Kåre — Turn on or off whether she can look up facts with Miss Library. She has one fixed personality (the same in chat, in the portrait night job and in the reflection meeting), and it follows the language chosen for the user.
innst_agenter.item_3: Tool matrix — Adjust which tools are allowed per user role. Changes take effect immediately.
innst_agenter.item_4: Model guard (Expert) — The box between KTSB and the language model. Shows each rule with its hit counts for the last 30 days and the latest hits. Each rule has one switch per part of KTSB that uses it (chat, reflection, Miss Library, Mechanic, dev slot): Off, Shadow (logs only, corrects nothing — how new rules and new parts are measured) or On. Applies from the next message.

innst_varsler.title: Settings → Notifications
innst_varsler.summary: Alert thresholds, quiet hours, and push
innst_varsler.body: Controls when and how Kåre notifies you about something unusual — from a quiet chat message to an immediate speaker announcement.
innst_varsler.item_1: Master switch — Turn the notification system on or off globally.
innst_varsler.item_2: Push target — A Home Assistant notify entity that receives push notifications for critical events.
innst_varsler.item_3: Thresholds — Minimum deviation score and minimum confidence an event must have to trigger an alert.
innst_varsler.item_4: Camera filter — Restrict which cameras can trigger alerts.

bruker_chat.title: Chat (Home page)
bruker_chat.item_1: Text field — Type your message and press Enter or the Send button.
bruker_chat.item_2: Voice button — Hold to speak. Kåre transcribes and responds by voice.
bruker_chat.item_3: Images — Drag and drop an image into the chat, or click the image icon to analyse it.
bruker_chat.item_4: Miss Kåre panel — Shown below Kåre's response with side comments and alternative perspectives.
bruker_chat.item_5: Trace view — Press the arrow below a response to see which tools Kåre used.
bruker_chat.item_6: Timer alerts — When a timer fires, the notification appears directly in chat without you needing to ask. Kåre confirms delivery automatically.

bruker_refleksjoner.title: My reflections
bruker_refleksjoner.summary: Personal meeting minutes from Kåre's nightly meetings
bruker_refleksjoner.item_1: Shows all reflection meetings where you were the topic.
bruker_refleksjoner.item_2: PIN protection — Enter your PIN to read the content. Only you have access.
bruker_refleksjoner.item_3: Meeting minutes are stored locally and never sent to third parties.
bruker_refleksjoner.item_4: PIN buffering — Kåre remembers your PIN within the same browser session so you do not need to enter it for each meeting.

bruker_stemmeopplaasing.title: User Settings → Voice Unlock
bruker_stemmeopplaasing.summary: Protect personal data behind a phrase or PIN on voice nodes
bruker_stemmeopplaasing.item_1: Applies to mic nodes only (ESP32 and Wyoming satellites) — not text chat.
bruker_stemmeopplaasing.item_2: Choose a method: phrase, PIN, or both. Kåre recognises the phrase or spoken digits and opens a 2-minute session.
bruker_stemmeopplaasing.item_3: An active session gives Kåre access to memory, profile, cameras, and agents. The session resets automatically with each command.
bruker_stemmeopplaasing.item_4: «Global lists» — Notes (e.g. the shopping list) can be made available without unlocking, so the whole household can add items.
bruker_stemmeopplaasing.item_5: Say «lock» to close the session manually. The session closes automatically after 2 minutes without activity.

noder_kategorier.title: Categories — AUDIO / MULTI / DISPLAY
noder_kategorier.item_1: AUDIO — Speaker only. Kåre speaks and plays music through the node.
noder_kategorier.item_2: MULTI — Speaker and display. Shows content and speaks (e.g. Nest Hub with screen, Google TV).
noder_kategorier.item_3: DISPLAY — Display only. Shows images, text and video. No direct TTS audio from the node.

verktoy_ssh.title: SSH nodes
verktoy_ssh.body: SSH nodes are machines on the network that Kåre can run commands on. Configure here, use via the «ssh_kommando» tool in chat.
verktoy_ssh.item_1: Node type: Linux/standard SSH (port 22, optional user) or HA OS (port 2222, root, only ha-commands allowed).
verktoy_ssh.item_2: Allow sudo — Enable per node and add exactly which sudo commands are allowed. Only listed commands are accepted. Without your own sudo commands Mechanic can only read; a sudo command you add here may run even if it changes something (but never chained with ; && $( >).
verktoy_ssh.item_3: Test connection — Click the button to verify the SSH connection directly in the GUI.

verktoy_timer.title: Timer limits
verktoy_timer.item_1: Max active timers per user — Set the limit using the number field and the «Save» button. Default is 20.

noder_svar.title: Replies, buttons and ducking
noder_svar.summary: Where the reply goes, starting a node from Home Assistant, and music that is turned down
noder_svar.item_1: Audio out — a node can take the question on one device and speak the answer on another (e.g. a small voice button in a room and the Nest next to it). «Auto» works as before.
noder_svar.item_2: Image out — when Kåre shows something (camera image, Plex) without saying where, it goes to the screen where you are. No screen in the room: as before.
noder_svar.item_3: If the output does not answer (e.g. the Nest is off), Kåre says so on the node's own speaker — even a small one — or on this machine's speakers. Without a speaker: only in the reply text and the status light.
noder_svar.item_4: Start from Home Assistant — press «Learn», then a button in HA (Zigbee, Hue, Matter …). Zigbee events (zha_event) need an admin token in HA; otherwise buttons that are entities work, or the webhook.
noder_svar.item_5: Webhook — a secret key per node and a ready HA automation to paste. Works with any button and any token. «New key» makes the old one invalid.
noder_svar.item_6: Voice — silence and ducking (bottom of Nodes): when a recording stops — «Automatic» measures the microphone's own noise and your voice, «Fixed level» uses a number you set — and that whatever plays on the output is quieted from the press until the reply is done (radio paused, HA players turned down and back). Wyoming nodes always use automatic.
noder_svar.item_7: KTSB Direct — the machine KTSB runs on is always a node: choose its microphone, place, default user and Home Assistant button just like other nodes. Replies play on the machine's own speakers unless «Audio out» says otherwise.
noder_svar.item_8: Online status — the WiFi icon on each node card: green = the node answers now, red = it does not (unplugged, no power, «unavailable» in HA), grey = it cannot be checked (no IP, port or HA entity). Checked every 30 seconds while the Nodes page is open; hover for details.

innst_skjermer.title: Settings → Screens
innst_skjermer.summary: Live camera and recipes on TVs and screens
innst_skjermer.body: KTSB has its own screen page that can show a live camera and cards (e.g. a recipe) on TVs, Google TV, Chromecast, Nest Hub and browsers. One switch turns it all on or off; off means Kåre does not see these actions either. Ask Kåre: «show the doorbell live on the TV» (without «live» or another word for moving pictures, Kåre sends a still picture), «find a pancake recipe and show it on the kitchen screen».
innst_skjermer.item_1: The screen page is on — the main switch. Off: no screen shows KTSB's page, and Kåre does not have the actions.
innst_skjermer.item_2: Live camera → Minutes — how long a live camera stays before it stops by itself (default 2). The screen then goes back to how it was: standby, the app that was on, or the photo frame. Kåre can set another time each time.
innst_skjermer.item_3: Nodes → (screen) → Screen page → Largest video size — weak TVs often cannot do more than 1280×720; larger streams are scaled down by KTSB.
innst_skjermer.item_4: Screens without Cast (e.g. Samsung) — once: open the address shown in the node dialog in the screen's browser (with http:// in front), and enter the four-digit code from the screen in the node dialog. The code stops others on the network from seeing the camera.
innst_skjermer.item_5: A Chromecast behind another input (e.g. a game console) switches the TV over to itself when something is shown; KTSB cannot switch back — use the remote. Frigate RTSP port (Expert) is only used when a stream must be re-encoded.

rooms.missing_hint_gone: Home Assistant has no entity with this ID (deleted or renamed). Remove it, or point the alias at the new one.
rooms.missing_hint_orphan: HA only keeps a leftover of this — the integration no longer provides it (typically after a firmware update). Use the new entity on the same device.

camera_questions.title: Was it you?
camera_questions.intro: The camera was unsure who it was. One tick answers — the answer is yours only, and helps KTSB learn which face sensors can be trusted. «Private» means it was you, but nothing more is kept. «Skip» means KTSB asks a little less often. «Don't know» closes the question without anything being learned.
camera_questions.ask_theme: Kåre has thought about this for several nights: «{{text}}» — is that right?

questions_card.title: Who / What / Where?
questions_card.others_intro: Person events nobody has settled. You can say who it was for anyone in the household who has not turned camera tracking off; the person's own answer counts over yours.
questions_card.others_refused: Not saved (the person has turned tracking off or has answered themselves).
questions_card.no_event_image: No picture stored for this event.
questions_card.click_for_image: Click a question to see the picture.
